What is MCP?

MCP is an open protocol that enables AI models to securely interact with local and remote resources through standardized server implementations. This list focuses on production-ready and experimental MCP servers that extend AI capabilities through file access, database connections, API integrations, and other contextual services.

Clients

Checkout awesome-mcp-clients and glama.ai/mcp/clients.

Remote Servers

This list is for servers with a GitHub repo you install and run yourself. Looking for a hosted server you just connect to over a URL? See awesome-remote-mcp-servers.

Tutorials

  • Tool Definition Quality Score (TDQS)
  • Model Context Protocol (MCP) Quickstart
  • Setup Claude Desktop App to Use a SQLite Database

Community

  • Discord Server

Legend

  • programming language

    • 🐍 – Python codebase
    • 📇 – TypeScript (or JavaScript) codebase

    • 🍎 – For macOS
    • 🪟 – For Windows
    • 🐧 - For Linux

Note

Confused about Local 🏠 vs Cloud ☁️?

  • Use local when MCP server is talking to a locally installed software, e.g. taking control over Chrome browser.
  • Use cloud when MCP server is talking to remote APIs, e.g. weather API.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A curated index of production-ready and experimental servers implementing the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for AI models.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Awesome MCP Servers is a central repository that catalogs implementations of the Model Context Protocol, an open standard designed to securely connect AI models to external data sources and tools. The directory categorizes servers based on their capabilities, such as file access, database querying, and API integrations, making it easier for developers to find existing solutions. It includes both official implementations and community-driven projects written across various languages like Python and TypeScript. The repository also links out to tutorials, clients, and community hubs to support the broader ecosystem.
keyFeatures: Categorized server index: Organizes MCP server implementations logically by their capabilities and target integrations.
Language tagging: Clearly identifies the programming language (e.g., Python, TypeScript) used for each server implementation.
Official implementation highlights: Distinguishes between community experiments and production-ready, officially supported servers.
Ecosystem resources: Aggregates links to MCP clients, tutorials, and development tips alongside the server list.
Community integration: Connects developers to related Discord and Reddit communities for ongoing support and discussion.

useCases.title: AI context expansion
useCases.description: Developers seeking pre-built MCP servers to quickly connect Claude or other LLMs to local databases or APIs.

useCases.description: Enthusiasts looking to discover new tools, clients, and frameworks built around the Model Context Protocol.

useCases.title: Standardized integration testing
useCases.description: AI platform builders sourcing various MCP servers to test the compatibility and robustness of their clients.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: AI engineers, tool builders, and developers looking to extend the capabilities of language models through standardized protocols. It requires an understanding of how to run or deploy the listed server implementations.
